claims.text: The local catalog models the All Nippon Airlines Get in a Jet! 2000 campaign phase 1 source group as one row containing Marill at source index 195.
Bulbapedia says this Marill print was released through the All Nippon Airways Get in a Jet! 2000 campaign and was available to customers on domestic flights between July 1 and August 31, 2000.
Bulbapedia says customers had to mail two domestic boarding-pass stubs attached to special postcards to Media Factory by September 7, 2000 to receive the Marill promo.
Bulbapedia says the card features ANA 2000 campaign-specific border text identifying it as an ANA special 2000 version card.
Bulbapedia says the Marill artwork was later reprinted in the English Wizards Black Star Promos and Team Rocket sets, and in Japanese on the Pokemon Web release.
Bulbapedia credits the ANA Marill artwork to Ryuta Kusumi, while PokeBoon lists the illustrator as CR CG Gangs for the Get in a Jet! 2000 campaign Marill.

Bulbapedia describes CR CG gangs as the credited artist for multiple Unnumbered Promotional cards including Crystal Tower's Entei, Pichu, Pikachu, Suicune, and Larvitar, and says card design credits include Creatures, Inc. and Ryuta Kusumi.
Bulbapedia identifies the ANA Marill as a Water-type Basic Pokemon card with 50 HP and the Rollout attack.
Bulbapedia describes Marill as a water-mouse Pokemon introduced in Generation II and says it has a nearly waterproof fur coat and a buoyant, oil-filled tail used like a float.

As judged collector texture, ANA Get in a Jet! 2000 Marill matters because the physical redemption route is inseparable from the card: an airline campaign turned boarding passes into Pokemon provenance, while Marill made the route feel playful and approachable.

narrative.human_title: ANA Get in a Jet! 2000 Marill: boarding passes become Pokemon memory
narrative.why_it_matters: The ANA Marill works because it makes the route feel literal and tender. You flew domestic ANA, saved boarding-pass stubs, mailed a postcard to Media Factory, and out came a small blue Johto mascot with campaign text in its border. It is not just an airline logo pasted onto a card. It is travel turned into evidence, evidence turned into mail, and mail turned into a Pokemon object.

special_identification_instructions.summary: Identify Marill by ANA Get in a Jet! 2000 phase 1 route, domestic boarding-pass/postcard redemption, and ANA special 2000 version border text before trusting generic Marill memory.
steps: Confirm the object is Marill / マリル and the claimed route is All Nippon Airlines / All Nippon Airways Get in a Jet! 2000 campaign phase 1, July 1-August 31, 2000.
Preserve the redemption mechanics: two domestic boarding-pass stubs attached to a special postcard and mailed to Media Factory by September 7, 2000.
Inspect for ANA special 2000 version border text or equivalent readable campaign text on the card.

Separate this print from the 1998 ANA Get in a Jet! Double Chance Campaign, ANA Everyone's Happy Campaign cards, phase 2 Get in a Jet! 2000 Suicune, Southern Islands Marill, Team Rocket Marill, Pokemon Web Marill, English Wizards Black Star Marill, and generic Marill listings.
Preserve Ryuta Kusumi / CR CG gangs art context without treating illustrator credit as proof of campaign route.

Before spending or trade gating, require seller-controlled photos of front/back, ANA/campaign border text, surface, edges/corners, and slab label if graded; catalog identity is legible support, not physical truth.

narrative.why_it_matters: Marill is perfect for this ANA route because it makes the campaign feel friendly rather than corporate. The card is not just Water-type text and a cute Johto face. It is two domestic boarding-pass stubs, a special postcard, a September 7 Media Factory deadline, and the little thrill of Pokemon showing up after a trip. For an agent, the romance and the trap are the same: without the ANA route, this becomes just another Marill.
